title: Nasdaq Rises as SpaceX Shares Jump on Rumored Tesla Deal – Live Market Update
body:
Wall Street opened on a bullish note on Tuesday, with the Nasdaq Composite climbing 1.2% after Elon Musk’s SpaceX reported a surprise beat on quarterly revenue, driven largely by a surge in its artificial‑intelligence services. The upbeat earnings sparked a rally in SpaceX’s publicly traded shares, which jumped more than 9% in early trading, and lifted broader technology indices. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 posted modest gains, while bond yields slipped as investors digested the mixed macro data that followed the earnings surprise.

SpaceX’s earnings release revealed that the company generated $1.84 billion in revenue for the quarter, exceeding the $1.71 billion consensus estimate. The bulk of the upside came from its AI‑powered satellite‑internet platform, which now offers on‑demand processing power to enterprises seeking to run large language models and other compute‑intensive workloads. Analysts noted that the AI segment, still in its infancy, contributed roughly $250 million to the top line—a figure that surprised many given the company’s historically hardware‑centric focus. The firm also disclosed that it is in advanced talks with Tesla to integrate its AI compute capabilities into the automaker’s next‑generation autonomous‑driving stack, a partnership that could accelerate the commercialization of both firms’ technologies.

The market reaction was swift. SpaceX’s stock, which trades on a limited secondary market, surged past its previous high, prompting a wave of buying from tech‑focused funds that had been waiting for a catalyst. The Nasdaq’s 12‑month rally, which has been buoyed by strong earnings from semiconductor and cloud‑computing firms, received fresh momentum as investors reassessed the growth potential of AI‑centric infrastructure providers. In contrast, traditional energy stocks lagged, with oil prices slipping 2% after OPEC+ signaled a possible extension of production cuts later this year, adding a layer of uncertainty to the broader market outlook.

Beyond the immediate earnings beat, the broader financial community is parsing what SpaceX’s performance signals for the competitive landscape of AI hardware. The company’s ability to monetize its Starlink constellation for compute services challenges established players like Nvidia, AMD and Intel, which have long dominated the AI accelerator market. By leveraging a global network of low‑earth‑orbit satellites, SpaceX can offer low‑latency, high‑bandwidth connections that are attractive for edge‑AI applications, from autonomous vehicles to real‑time analytics in remote locations. Industry analysts suggest that if the Tesla partnership materialises, SpaceX could secure a foothold in the automotive AI supply chain, potentially reshaping the revenue mix of both firms.

Investors are also weighing the macroeconomic backdrop that accompanies the rally. The Federal Reserve’s latest policy statement hinted at a pause in rate hikes, citing modestly lower inflation readings, which helped lower the yield on the 10‑year Treasury to 3.78%. Lower borrowing costs tend to favor growth‑oriented stocks, reinforcing the upward drift in the Nasdaq. However, concerns linger over global supply‑chain bottlenecks and the lingering effects of geopolitical tensions in Eastern Europe, which could dampen corporate earnings in the coming quarters. Moreover, the surge in AI‑related spending raises questions about capital allocation, as companies balance the allure of cutting‑edge technology against the need for fiscal prudence.

Looking ahead, the market’s next move will likely hinge on a few key developments. First, confirmation of the SpaceX‑Tesla collaboration could act as a catalyst for further AI‑infrastructure investments, prompting other tech firms to explore satellite‑based compute solutions. Second, upcoming earnings reports from major AI chip manufacturers will test whether SpaceX’s model can sustain its revenue growth or remains a niche play. Finally, the Fed’s policy trajectory and any shifts in global energy supply will continue to shape investor sentiment across sectors. For now, the blend of strong corporate earnings and a cautiously optimistic macro environment has set the stage for a potentially prolonged rally in technology stocks, with SpaceX’s AI breakthrough serving as a focal point for market participants.
